themes_detail.label: Illegal Posting Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints surged to 5 THIS WEEK compared to a 0.1 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 3,900% spike (z-score: 14.74)—suggesting a coordinated posting campaign or sudden enforcement gap in Central Harlem.
evidence: 5 illegal posting complaints THIS WEEK vs 0.1 weekly baseline (3,900% increase)
Z-score of 14.74 indicates statistically extreme anomaly
Last week also showed elevated complaints (5 total), suggesting sustained trend, not one-off
reporting_angles: What triggered the posting surge—is it political, commercial, or gang-related tagging?
Has the city's posting removal contractor reduced frequency or staffing in Central Harlem?

themes_detail.label: Encampment Surge
themes_detail.summary: Homeless encampment complaints jumped to 17 THIS WEEK versus a 4.9 weekly average over 8 weeks—a 249% spike (z-score: 3.72)—coinciding with repeated CB budget requests for homeless facility upgrades, suggesting strain on existing shelter capacity.
evidence: 17 encampment complaints THIS WEEK vs 4.9 weekly baseline (249% increase, z-score: 3.72)
Community Board has submitted 'Upgrade existing facilities for the homeless' budget request repeatedly (unsolved, year-over-year)
Recent Gothamist coverage (2026-04-07) on Legionnaires' outbreak suggests ongoing health/facility issues in district
reporting_angles: Are encampments concentrated in specific neighborhoods (subway stations, parks, commercial corridors)?
What is the wait time for shelter intake, and has DHS capacity in Harlem decreased recently?

themes_detail.label: Graffiti & Vandalism Wave
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints spiked to 7 LAST WEEK from a 0.6 weekly average—a 1,020% increase (z-score: 7.44)—paired with the illegal posting surge, signaling either a coordinated vandalism campaign or breakdown in street maintenance response.
evidence: 7 graffiti complaints LAST WEEK vs 0.6 weekly baseline (1,020% increase, z-score: 7.44)
Converges with 3,900% spike in illegal posting THIS WEEK—suggests coordinated street disorder or enforcement gap
44 street condition complaints LAST WEEK (354% above 8-week avg of 8.4) further indicates deteriorating streetscape
reporting_angles: Are graffiti and posting complaints concentrated in the same blocks or neighborhoods?
Has the Parks Department or Sanitation scaled back graffiti removal crews in Central Harlem?

themes_detail.label: Street Condition Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints reached 38 LAST WEEK versus an 8.4 weekly average—a 354% spike (z-score: 3.06)—aligning with CB budget requests for Parks equipment upgrades and suggesting accelerating pavement, pothole, or sidewalk failures.
evidence: 38 street condition complaints LAST WEEK vs 8.4 weekly baseline (354% increase, z-score: 3.06)
Community Board has repeatedly requested 'New equipment for maintenance' from Parks Dept (unsolved, year-over-year)
Convergence with graffiti and posting spikes suggests overall streetscape maintenance crisis, not isolated issue
reporting_angles: Which streets or intersections are generating the most complaints—are they high-traffic corridors or residential side streets?
What is the current Parks maintenance crew capacity and budget allocation in CD 110 vs other Harlem districts?

themes_detail.label: Vendor Enforcement Spike
themes_detail.summary: Vendor enforcement complaints jumped to 5 THIS WEEK from a 0.2 weekly baseline—a 1,900% spike (z-score: 7.18)—indicating either a sudden crackdown or proliferation of unauthorized street vending in Central Harlem.
evidence: 5 vendor enforcement complaints THIS WEEK vs 0.2 weekly baseline (1,900% increase, z-score: 7.18)
Spike mirrors timing of illegal posting and encampment surges, all THIS WEEK
May reflect either aggressive enforcement or rapid growth in unlicensed vending activity
reporting_angles: Is this driven by aggressive enforcement (new initiative or reassigned personnel) or an actual surge in street vendors?
Are complaints concentrated near transit hubs, commercial strips, or food markets?
